title.narrative: Sustainable Hydrosystems: Integrating Ecohydrology and Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) into Inclusive Water Resource Management

description.narrative: Recognizing the significance of local ecological knowledge (LEK), as demonstrated by traditional practices such as Bali's Subak system, becomes imperative in fostering sustainable integrated water resource management (IWRM), underscores the importance of considering social, environmental, and economic factors. In this context, Ecohydrology, combining hydrological and biological processes, is crucial for ensuring water security and biodiversity in Indonesia. To achieve this, a proposed project aims to enhance knowledge co-production between Ecohydrology and LEK, aiming to improve integrated water resource management. The project aims to develop a framework strategy and improve Ecohydrology adoption, emphasizing stakeholder engagement through workshops and seminars.
